<section id="A6.SS5" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">F.5 </span>Synthetic Many Class: Critical Difference Diagram</h3>

<figure id="A6.F36" class="ltx_figure"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2605.13986v2/tabarena_many_class_100_v2__roc_auc__cd_scikit_posthocs.svg" id="A6.F36.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/202;" width="476" height="202"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="A6.F36.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 36</span>: </span><span id="A6.F36.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">Critical difference diagram for ROC AUC on the synthetic
many-class benchmark (up to 100 classes).<span id="A6.F36.5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium">
TabPFN-3 is top-ranked on every (dataset, split) pair and ranks significantly ahead of all baselines. Bars connect methods whose rank differences are not statistically significant at <math id="A6.F36.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha=0.05" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.05</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha=0.05</annotation></semantics></math> under a Conover-Friedman post-hoc test <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib154" title="" class="ltx_ref">78</a>]</cite>.
</span></span></figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A7" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix G </span>Supplementary Inference Time Details</h2>

<section id="A7.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">G.1 </span>Compilation and FlashAttention-3</h3>

<div id="A7.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A7.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A7.SS1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text">TabPFN-3</span> is shipped with two opt-in performance features that target different bottlenecks: <span id="A7.SS1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">torch.compile</span> and FlashAttention-3. At the shapes relevant to large-data inference, the bulk of forward-pass cost is dispatch overhead and attention compute, and the speed-ups of <span id="A7.SS1.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">torch.compile</span> and FlashAttention-3 compose cleanly with our chunking strategy without changing the model’s behaviour.</p>
</div>
<section id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">torch.compile.</h5>

<div id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Three hot-path methods are wrapped with <span id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">@torch.compile(dynamic=True)</span>: feature preprocessing plus embedding grouping, the column-chunk processing block (used in the non-row-chunked path), and the row-chunk processing block (used when chunking is enabled). The <span id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">dynamic=True</span> mode keeps a single compiled graph across batch and feature-count variation, so the same compiled artefact serves the whole inference grid without re-tracing.</p>
</div>
<div id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Figure <a href="#A7.F37.sf1" title="Figure 37(a) ‣ Figure 37 ‣ torch.compile. ‣ G.1 Compilation and FlashAttention-3 ‣ Appendix G Supplementary Inference Time Details" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">37(a)</span></a> shows the wall-clock impact on MI-250x. The y-axis is <math id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T_{\mathrm{eager}}/T_{\mathrm{compile}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>T</mi><mi>eager</mi></msub><mo>/</mo><msub><mi>T</mi><mi>compile</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T_{\mathrm{eager}}/T_{\mathrm{compile}}</annotation></semantics></math>, so a value above 1 means compile is faster on that shape; each marker is annotated with the absolute time. <span id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">torch.compile</span> fuses Python-level dispatch into single kernel calls, so it helps most where dispatch is the bottleneck: as <math id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n_{\mathrm{features}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>features</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n_{\mathrm{features}}</annotation></semantics></math> grows, more tensor work becomes compile-able per call. In the non-chunked series the speed-up climbs from <math id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1.04" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1.04</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.04</annotation></semantics></math>–<math id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.m4" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="1.15{\times}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1.15</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.15{\times}</annotation></semantics></math> at <math id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n_{\mathrm{features}}=10" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>features</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n_{\mathrm{features}}=10</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1.10" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1.10</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.10</annotation></semantics></math>–<math id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.m7" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="1.46{\times}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1.46</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.46{\times}</annotation></semantics></math> at <math id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n_{\mathrm{features}}=100" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>features</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>100</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n_{\mathrm{features}}=100</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1.40" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1.40</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.40</annotation></semantics></math>–<math id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.m10" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="1.58{\times}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1.58</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.58{\times}</annotation></semantics></math> at <math id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n_{\mathrm{features}}=500" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>features</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>500</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n_{\mathrm{features}}=500</annotation></semantics></math>. The chunked series shows the same direction with a different shape: chunking already amortises some dispatch overhead by batching the inner loop, so compile’s marginal benefit is largest at small <math id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n_{\mathrm{train}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>train</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n_{\mathrm{train}}</annotation></semantics></math> (<math id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1.21" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1.21</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.21</annotation></semantics></math>–<math id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.m14" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="1.43{\times}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1.43</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.43{\times}</annotation></semantics></math> at <math id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n_{\mathrm{train}}=10^{3}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>train</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n_{\mathrm{train}}=10^{3}</annotation></semantics></math>) and large <math id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n_{\mathrm{features}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>features</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n_{\mathrm{features}}</annotation></semantics></math> and converges toward parity (<math id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.95" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.95</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.95</annotation></semantics></math>–<math id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.m18" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="1.06{\times}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1.06</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.06{\times}</annotation></semantics></math>) at <math id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.m19" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n_{\mathrm{train}}\geq 10^{5}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>train</mi></msub><mo>≥</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>5</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n_{\mathrm{train}}\geq 10^{5}</annotation></semantics></math> for the smaller feature counts, where the residual cost is dominated by attention itself and compile has no further headroom to claim.</p>
</div>

<section id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">FlashAttention-3.</h5>

<div id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">FlashAttention-3 (FA3) <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib142" title="" class="ltx_ref">35</a>]</cite> is a Hopper-specific attention kernel that delivers higher throughput and lower memory use than the generic Scaled Dot-Product Attention (SDPA) path. Attention dominates the forward-pass cost of large-<math id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n_{\mathrm{train}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>train</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n_{\mathrm{train}}</annotation></semantics></math> inference, so even a constant-factor improvement in the attention kernel translates into a meaningful end-to-end speed-up. We therefore expose FA3 as an auto-detecting backend: on Hopper-class GPUs with the FA3 library installed, the in-context-learning self-attention – which carries the bulk of the attention cost at large <math id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n_{\mathrm{train}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>train</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n_{\mathrm{train}}</annotation></semantics></math> – is routed through FA3, while attention sites whose head dimensions are not FA3-eligible silently fall back to SDPA. On non-Hopper devices (consumer Ada, AMD MI-250x, Blackwell) the same dispatcher selects SDPA.</p>
</div>
<div id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Figure <a href="#A7.F37.sf2" title="Figure 37(b) ‣ Figure 37 ‣ torch.compile. ‣ G.1 Compilation and FlashAttention-3 ‣ Appendix G Supplementary Inference Time Details" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">37(b)</span></a> shows the H100 SDPA-versus-auto comparison in ratio form. The y-axis is <math id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T_{\mathrm{sdpa}}/T_{\mathrm{auto}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>T</mi><mi>sdpa</mi></msub><mo>/</mo><msub><mi>T</mi><mi>auto</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T_{\mathrm{sdpa}}/T_{\mathrm{auto}}</annotation></semantics></math>, so a value above 1 means FA3 is faster than SDPA on that shape; each marker is annotated with the absolute auto time so the magnitude being sped up is recoverable.
The pattern matches the FA3 design profile. At small training sets (<math id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n_{\mathrm{train}}\leq 1000" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>train</mi></msub><mo>≤</mo><mn>1000</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n_{\mathrm{train}}\leq 1000</annotation></semantics></math>) the FA3 dispatch and kernel-launch overhead exceeds the per-call attention work, and SDPA is 10–15% faster (<math id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T_{\mathrm{sdpa}}/T_{\mathrm{auto}}\approx 0.84\text{--}0.91" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>T</mi><mi>sdpa</mi></msub><mo>/</mo><msub><mi>T</mi><mi>auto</mi></msub></mrow><mo>≈</mo><mrow><mn>0.84</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mtext>–</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mn>0.91</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T_{\mathrm{sdpa}}/T_{\mathrm{auto}}\approx 0.84\text{--}0.91</annotation></semantics></math> across feature counts). The cross-over arrives sooner the smaller <math id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n_{\mathrm{features}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>features</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n_{\mathrm{features}}</annotation></semantics></math>: by <math id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n_{\mathrm{train}}=10^{4}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>train</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>4</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n_{\mathrm{train}}=10^{4}</annotation></semantics></math> FA3 wins at <math id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n_{\mathrm{features}}=10" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>features</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n_{\mathrm{features}}=10</annotation></semantics></math> (<math id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2.m7" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="1.21{\times}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1.21</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.21{\times}</annotation></semantics></math>), is roughly even at <math id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n_{\mathrm{features}}=100" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>features</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>100</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n_{\mathrm{features}}=100</annotation></semantics></math> (<math id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2.m9" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="1.07{\times}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1.07</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.07{\times}</annotation></semantics></math>), and at parity at <math id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n_{\mathrm{features}}=500" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>features</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>500</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n_{\mathrm{features}}=500</annotation></semantics></math> (<math id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2.m11" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="1.02{\times}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1.02</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.02{\times}</annotation></semantics></math>). At the inference shapes we care about (<math id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n_{\mathrm{train}}\geq 10^{5}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>train</mi></msub><mo>≥</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>5</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n_{\mathrm{train}}\geq 10^{5}</annotation></semantics></math>) FA3 is the clear win across all feature counts, with the speed-up climbing to <math id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1.49" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1.49</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.49</annotation></semantics></math>–<math id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2.m14" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="1.73{\times}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1.73</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.73{\times}</annotation></semantics></math> at <math id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n_{\mathrm{train}}=10^{6}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>train</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>6</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n_{\mathrm{train}}=10^{6}</annotation></semantics></math>. Chunking does not interact with the FA3-versus-SDPA comparison: the chunked and non-chunked curves overlap to within run-to-run noise, since chunking changes the outer dispatch loop but leaves the underlying attention-kernel selection intact.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A7.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">G.2 </span>Interpretability: SHAP-Value Computation</h3>

<div id="A7.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A7.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">TabPFN-3’s improved, smaller KV cache (Section <a href="#S2.SS4.SSS2" title="2.4.2 Fast Inference with a Small KV-cache ‣ 2.4 Inference Optimization ‣ 2 TabPFN-3" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.4.2</span></a>) can speed up the computation of SHAP values by multiple order of magnitudes. This is because imputation-based approaches to SHAP-value computation reuse the same <span id="A7.SS2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">fit</span> on many different forward passes. <a href="#A7.F38" title="Figure 38 ‣ G.2 Interpretability: SHAP-Value Computation ‣ Appendix G Supplementary Inference Time Details" class="ltx_ref ltx_refmacro_autoref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure 38</span></a> shows the efficiency gains users can expect from enabling the KV cache during SHAP-value-computation.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A7.F38" class="ltx_figure">
<div class="ltx_flex_figure">
<div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_2">
<figure id="A7.F38.fig1" class="ltx_figure ltx_figure_panel ltx_align_center"><img src="2605.13986v2/shap_kv_cache_speedup_heatmap_baseline.png" id="A7.F38.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/310;" width="476" height="310" alt="Refer to caption">
</figure></div><div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_2">

<section id="A9" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix I </span>TabPFN Use Case Overview</h2>

<div id="A9.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A9.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Previous TabPFN models have been applied to a broad set of use cases. We now list 201 published use cases across different industries.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="Ax2" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix">Highlights</h2>

<div id="Ax2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="Ax2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We highlight a selection of representative use cases that demonstrate TabPFN’s strengths across domains:</p>
<ol id="Ax2.I1" class="ltx_enumerate">
<li id="Ax2.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">1.</span> 
<div id="Ax2.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="Ax2.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">TabPFN enabled non-invasive early detection of pancreatic cancer by integrating NMR metabolomics with clinical and protein biomarkers <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib157" title="" class="ltx_ref">79</a>]</cite>. <a href="https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-026-69426-9" title="" class="ltx_ref ltx_href">Link</a></p>
</div></li>
<li id="Ax2.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">2.</span> 
<div id="Ax2.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="Ax2.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">TabPFN provided highly accurate predictions of donor mobilization success using baseline and post-mobilization variables, facilitating early triage and improved transplantation outcomes <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib182" title="" class="ltx_ref">80</a>]</cite>. <a href="https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jtct.2026.02.016" title="" class="ltx_ref ltx_href">Link</a></p>
</div></li>
<li id="Ax2.I1.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">3.</span> 
<div id="Ax2.I1.i3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="Ax2.I1.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">TabPFN was used for effective differentiation between psychotic and non-psychotic major depression, improving classification accuracy and supporting psychiatric diagnosis <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib189" title="" class="ltx_ref">81</a>]</cite>. <a href="https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jad.2026.121454" title="" class="ltx_ref ltx_href">Link</a></p>
</div></li>
<li id="Ax2.I1.i4" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">4.</span> 
<div id="Ax2.I1.i4.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="Ax2.I1.i4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">TabPFN served as a high-fidelity surrogate model for optimizing geopolymer concrete mix design, achieving superior accuracy, generalization, and low-uncertainty predictions compared to other ML approaches <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib223" title="" class="ltx_ref">82</a>]</cite>. <a href="https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-025-29088-x" title="" class="ltx_ref ltx_href">Link</a></p>
</div></li>
<li id="Ax2.I1.i5" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">5.</span> 
<div id="Ax2.I1.i5.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="Ax2.I1.i5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">TabPFN enabled robust prediction of silica nanoparticle cytotoxicity <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib159" title="" class="ltx_ref">83</a>]</cite>. <a href="https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-025-33872-0" title="" class="ltx_ref ltx_href">Link</a></p>
</div></li>
<li id="Ax2.I1.i6" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">6.</span> 
<div id="Ax2.I1.i6.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">

<section id="Ax4" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix">Financial Services, Banking, and Insurance</h2>

<div id="Ax4.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="Ax4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We collected 7 published TabPFN use cases in this area. These applications include risk modeling, actuarial analysis, credit-related prediction, and customer analytics.</p>
</div>
<div id="Ax4.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<ol id="Ax4.I3" class="ltx_enumerate">

<p id="Ax4.I3.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">TabPFN improves low-supervision transaction analytics by doubling zero-shot MCC on churn prediction and enhancing few-shot MCC, enabling better knowledge-grounded reasoning in financial transaction analysis <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib207" title="" class="ltx_ref">180</a>]</cite>. <a href="http://arxiv.org/abs/2603.15459" title="" class="ltx_ref ltx_href">Link</a></p>

<section id="Ax7" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix">Other Industries</h2>

<div id="Ax7.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="Ax7.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We collected 31 further published TabPFN use cases in this area, spanning a heterogeneous set of domains and prediction tasks.</p>
</div>
<div id="Ax7.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<ol id="Ax7.I6" class="ltx_enumerate">
<li id="Ax7.I6.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">1.</span> 
<div id="Ax7.I6.i1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="Ax7.I6.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">TabPFN enables the construction of credal sets for models where it was previously infeasible, broadening uncertainty representation and improving uncertainty estimation <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib251" title="" class="ltx_ref">246</a>]</cite>. <a href="http://arxiv.org/abs/2603.08495v1" title="" class="ltx_ref ltx_href">Link</a></p>
</div></li>
<li id="Ax7.I6.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">2.</span> 
<div id="Ax7.I6.i2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="Ax7.I6.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">TabPFN enables efficient and valid hypothesis testing for feature relevance in tabular data, allowing accurate statistical inference in nonlinear and correlated settings <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib252" title="" class="ltx_ref">247</a>]</cite>. <a href="http://arxiv.org/abs/2603.06609v1" title="" class="ltx_ref ltx_href">Link</a></p>

<div id="Ax7.I6.i3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="Ax7.I6.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">TabPFN enables efficient computation of conditional Shapley values, resulting in faster and often more accurate explainable AI analysis <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib253" title="" class="ltx_ref">248</a>]</cite>. <a href="http://arxiv.org/abs/2602.09489v1" title="" class="ltx_ref ltx_href">Link</a></p>

<p id="Ax7.I6.i4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">TabPFN enables effective node classification by leveraging engineered tabular features from graph data as a practical and competitive alternative to graph-specific and language-based foundation models <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib254" title="" class="ltx_ref">249</a>]</cite>. <a href="http://arxiv.org/abs/2512.08798v1" title="" class="ltx_ref ltx_href">Link</a></p>

<p id="Ax7.I6.i5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">TabPFN was integrated as the surrogate model enabling accurate and efficient prediction with uncertainty estimation, enhancing the performance, scalability, and zero-shot transfer capability of the DB-SAEA framework <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib255" title="" class="ltx_ref">250</a>]</cite>. <a href="http://arxiv.org/abs/2511.15551v1" title="" class="ltx_ref ltx_href">Link</a></p>

<p id="Ax7.I6.i6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">TabPFN was used to model the relationship between nuclear structure properties and <math id="Ax7.I6.i6.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>α</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha</annotation></semantics></math>-particle preformation factors, improving <math id="Ax7.I6.i6.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>α</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha</annotation></semantics></math>-decay half-life predictions and enabling insights into nuclear shell effects and magic numbers <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib256" title="" class="ltx_ref">251</a>]</cite>. <a href="http://arxiv.org/abs/2511.14705v1" title="" class="ltx_ref ltx_href">Link</a></p>

<p id="Ax7.I6.i30.p1.1" class="ltx_p">TabPFN was used in forensic science to advance biogeographical ancestry predictions <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib19" title="" class="ltx_ref">275</a>]</cite>. <a href="https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1872497325000705" title="" class="ltx_ref ltx_href">Link</a></p>
</div></li>
<li id="Ax7.I6.i31" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">31.</span> 
<div id="Ax7.I6.i31.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="Ax7.I6.i31.p1.1" class="ltx_p">TabPFN was used as a benchmark model for predicting avocado alternate bearing from Sentinel-2 and climate features <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib134" title="" class="ltx_ref">276</a>]</cite>. <a href="https://www.preprints.org/manuscript/202510.2413" title="" class="ltx_ref ltx_href">Link</a></p>
</div></li>
</ol>
